Here is a Semgrep YAML rule that matches the vulnerable behavior and avoids matching the patched behavior:

```yaml
---
id: vuln-felix-dev-87513ea3
title: "Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')"
description: "The application is vulnerable to Cross Site Scripting (XSS) attacks due to improper encoding or sanitizing user inputs."
severity: WARNING
language: java

patterns:
  - name: improper-encoding
    meta:
      category: VULNERABILITY
      framework: FELIX_DEV
      id: 87513ea3
    pattern: >
      :xss:`this` = `this`.getParameter("FILTER_PARAM");
---
```

This rule will match the vulnerable function or method if it directly assigns user input to a variable without proper encoding. The taint-mode field is not necessary for this type of rule, as Semgrep can automatically detect when user inputs are used in a dangerous way.
